result.title: Out of Sight, Not Out of Clues: Can Video LLMs Guess from Partial Evidence?
result.summary: In real-world applications like egocentric recording, visual accessibility, and surveillance review, visual evidence for Video Large Language Models (Video LLMs) is often only partially captured. A reliable model should match its response to the evidence: answering when sufficient, guessing from visible clues when partial, and abstaining when absent. Yet existing benchmarks enforce a binary answerable-or-unanswerable split, leaving partial evidence unmeasured and obscuring whether failures arise from missing evidence or misjudging sufficiency. We introduce ClueProbe, a diagnostic benchmark to (1) separate perceiving evidence from judging sufficiency, and (2) validate our diagnosis via targeted fine-tuning. ClueProbe comprises 1,721 human-annotated questions across 598 natural videos, labeled Answerable, Guessable, or Unanswerable, alongside controlled perturbations altering wording or visual input. Evaluating 10 open-source and proprietary Video LLMs reveals that failures stem from judgment rather than perception: models perceive the evidence yet lack graded sufficiency awareness, answering or refusing outright while rarely guessing from partial clues. Targeted fine-tuning shows that this reflects missing supervision rather than insufficient capacity: supervising the guess level lifts appropriate guessing from 1.6% to 40.4% without extra false refusals, whereas conventional refusal tuning rejects 92% of guessable questions. Data and code will be released at https://github.com/suat-llm/ClueProbe.

AI.brief_summary: 论文提出诊断基准 ClueProbe，含 598 段视频上 1,721 个标注为「可答／可猜／不可答」三档的人工问题及措辞与视觉扰动，评测 10 个开源与闭源 Video LLM，并通过只监督「猜」档的定向微调验证失败源于监督缺失而非能力不足。
AI.relevance_reason: 直接对应视觉证据筛选与 STOP 决策：其证据充足度的分级判定（拒绝 92% 可猜题、监督后猜答率 1.6%→40.4%）可供核查「感知到证据但不会用」与 latent 状态中证据保留、停止判断之间的对应关系，但属视频基准与外层行为度量，不涉及内部 latent 机制。
